source.text: וְאַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה בְּמַלְכ֖וּת אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֣סְתְּא מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרָ֑ס עֶזְרָא֙ בֶּן־שְׂרָיָ֔ה בֶּן־עֲזַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after these things, in [the] reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,

en.L: And after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
en.B: After these events, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
en.R: Many years after this, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, there was a man named Ezra. His family line went back through Seraiah, Azariah, Hilkiah,

decisions.choice: Artaxerxes king of Persia: most likely Artaxerxes I, who reigned 465-424 BC
decisions.reason: Three Persian kings bore this name. The king who sent Ezra is most likely Artaxerxes I, the king Nehemiah served (Nehemiah 2:1), so that the seventh year of verse 7 is 458 BC. Some date Ezra's journey to the seventh year of Artaxerxes II (398 BC), placing him after Nehemiah; the text itself names only Artaxerxes.

decisions.choice: after these things: after the temple was finished, a gap of nearly sixty years
decisions.reason: The phrase links the new section loosely to what went before. The temple was completed in the sixth year of Darius (6:15, 516/515 BC); if the king here is Artaxerxes I, Ezra arrives in 458 BC, so the book passes over almost sixty years without comment. This is the first time Ezra himself appears in the book that bears his name.

decisions.choice: son of Seraiah: a descendant of Seraiah, not his child
decisions.reason: Seraiah was the chief priest whom Nebuchadnezzar put to death at Riblah in 587/586 BC (2 Kings 25:18-21), more than 125 years before Ezra's journey. In a priestly line, "son of" can mean descendant. The list traces Ezra back to Aaron (verse 5) to show that he belongs to the high-priestly family.

decisions.choice: Many years after this
decisions.reason: Readable makes the long gap after chapter 6 explicit, so a new reader does not think Ezra came right after the temple was finished. It turns the list of names that follows into a family line rather than a chain of "son of".

source.text: בֶּן־שַׁלּ֥וּם בֶּן־צָד֖וֹק בֶּן־אֲחִיטֽוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,

en.L: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
en.B: son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
en.R: Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub,

decisions.choice: Zadok: a later priest of the same name, in the line of Solomon's Zadok
decisions.reason: The list in 1 Chronicles 5:29-41 (6:3-15 in the numbering many Bibles use) names two priests called Zadok, each a son of an Ahitub. This one, the father of Shallum, belongs to the later generations (1 Chronicles 5:38); the line as a whole goes back to the Zadok who served under David and Solomon (1 Kings 1:39; 2:35).

source.text: בֶּן־אֲמַרְיָ֥ה בֶן־עֲזַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־מְרָיֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,

en.L: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
en.B: son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
en.R: Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth,

decisions.choice: a shortened line: between Azariah and Meraioth several generations are left out
decisions.reason: In the fuller priestly list of 1 Chronicles 5:32-37 (6:6-11 in the numbering many Bibles use), six names stand between Meraioth and the Azariah who comes after Amariah. Ezra's list leaves them out, as ancient genealogies often did; it aims to show descent, not to name every generation.

source.text: בֶּן־זְרַֽחְיָ֥ה בֶן־עֻזִּ֖י בֶּן־בֻּקִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,

en.L: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
en.B: son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
en.R: Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki,

source.text: בֶּן־אֲבִישׁ֗וּעַ בֶּן־פִּֽינְחָס֙ בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֔ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֥ן הַכֹּהֵ֖ן הָרֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, the head,

en.L: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the head priest,
en.B: son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest,
en.R: Abishua, Phinehas and Eleazar, all the way back to Aaron, the first chief priest.

decisions.choice: Aaron the head priest: the high priest, from whom every priest descended
decisions.reason: Aaron was the first high priest (Exodus 28:1; Leviticus 8), and the priesthood passed through his son Eleazar and grandson Phinehas, to whom God promised a lasting priesthood (Numbers 25:10-13). By ending the list with Aaron, the writer presents Ezra as a priest of the purest line, fit to teach the law and handle the temple's gifts.

decisions.choice: all the way back to Aaron, the first chief priest
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the list is doing, and adds "first" because Aaron is named as the head of the whole priestly line.

source.text: ה֤וּא עֶזְרָא֙ עָלָ֣ה מִבָּבֶ֔ל וְהֽוּא־סֹפֵ֤ר מָהִיר֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֶּן־ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ כְּיַד־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עָלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל בַּקָּשָׁתֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: he, Ezra, went up from Babylon, and he [was] a scribe skilled in [the] law of Moses, which had given YHWH [the] God of Israel; and gave to him the king, according to [the] hand of YHWH his God upon him, all his request.

en.L: this Ezra went up from Babylon. And he was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel had given. And the king gave him all his request, according to the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God upon him.
en.B: this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe well versed in the law of Moses, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel had given. The king granted him everything he asked, because the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God was on him.
en.R: Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylon. He was a teacher of the law, and he knew well the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, had given through Moses. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} his God was helping him, so the king gave him everything he asked for.

decisions.choice: a skilled scribe: an expert in the written law, not only a copyist
decisions.reason: The word for scribe first meant a writer or secretary (2 Samuel 8:17), but by Ezra's time it names a man learned in the Scriptures who copies, studies and explains them (verses 10-11). "Skilled" is the word used of the "ready scribe" of Psalm 45:2 and the skillful worker of Proverbs 22:29: quick and expert.

decisions.choice: the hand of YHWH his God upon him: God's favor and power working for him
decisions.reason: God's hand being upon someone is a picture of his help and protection. Ezra uses the phrase as a refrain (7:9, 28; 8:18, 22, 31) to say that the king's generosity and the safe journey came from God, not from Ezra's skill or the king's goodwill alone.

decisions.choice: went up: travelled to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Going to Jerusalem is always going "up" in Hebrew, both because the city stands in the hills and because it is the place of God's house. The same verb is used of the first returns (1:3; 2:1).

decisions.choice: a teacher of the law (Readable); a scribe (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: To most readers today a scribe is someone who copies writing. Readable says what Ezra was, a teacher of the law, and keeps that wording through the book; Literal and Balanced keep "scribe".

decisions.choice: God's help stated before the king's gift
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cause first, so the short sentences show plainly that the king's generosity came from God's help.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲל֣וּ מִבְּנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל וּמִן־הַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֜ם וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֧ים וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֛ים וְהַנְּתִינִ֖ים אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֖בַע לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥סְתְּא הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up some of [the] sons of Israel and some of the priests and the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim to Jerusalem, in [the] year seven of Artaxerxes the king.

en.L: And some of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and some of the priests and the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
en.B: Some of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as well as some of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants, also went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
en.R: In the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king, a group of {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went with him to Jerusalem. Among them were priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim: the temple servants
decisions.reason: The word means "those given", people given to the temple to do its heavy work under the Levites (8:20; compare Joshua 9:27). They appear in the lists of the first return (2:43-58).

decisions.choice: the seventh year of Artaxerxes: 458 BC, if the king is Artaxerxes I
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 1. Verses 8-9 date the journey within this year.

decisions.choice: went with him
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit what the setting implies: these people travelled with Ezra (8:1).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֑י הִ֛יא שְׁנַ֥ת הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖ית לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came [to] Jerusalem in the fifth month; it [was] the seventh year of the king.

en.L: And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month; that was the seventh year of the king.
en.B: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king's seventh year.
en.R: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of that year.

decisions.choice: the fifth month: the month later called Ab, in midsummer (July to August)
decisions.reason: Months are counted from the spring new year (Exodus 12:2). The journey began in the first month (verse 9), the time of Passover.

source.text: כִּ֗י בְּאֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן ה֣וּא יְסֻ֔ד הַֽמַּעֲלָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל וּבְאֶחָ֞ד לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֗י בָּ֚א אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כְּיַד־אֱלֹהָ֖יו הַטּוֹבָ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: For on [day] one of the first month that [was] the beginning of the going up from Babylon, and on [day] one of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to [the] hand of his God, the good, upon him.

en.L: For on the first of the first month he began the going up from Babylon, and on the first of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
en.B: He had set the first day of the first month for the departure from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he arrived in Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was on him.
en.R: He had planned to leave Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month. His God was kind to him and helped him.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the going up: the day the departure was fixed or began
decisions.reason: The noun means a foundation or beginning; read with a slightly different vowel it is a verb, "he fixed". Either way the first of the first month marks the start of the journey. Ezra's own account says the company gathered at the Ahava canal and set out on the twelfth day (8:15, 31), so this date is the start of the process rather than the day they left the camp.

decisions.choice: four months on the road
decisions.reason: From the first day of the first month to the first day of the fifth is about four months, for a journey of some 900 miles by the route along the Euphrates, travelling with families, flocks and treasure (8:21, 26-27).

decisions.choice: the good hand of his God upon him
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 6. "Good" adds that God's hand was kind: it gave help, not judgment (8:18, 22).

source.text: כִּ֤י עֶזְרָא֙ הֵכִ֣ין לְבָב֔וֹ לִדְר֛וֹשׁ אֶת־תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה וְלַעֲשֹׂ֑ת וּלְלַמֵּ֥ד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֹ֥ק וּמִשְׁפָּֽט׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the law of YHWH and to do [it] and to teach in Israel statute and judgment.

en.L: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to do it, and to teach in Israel statute and judgment.
en.B: For Ezra had set his heart to study the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and rulings in Israel.
en.R: This was because Ezra had made up his mind to study the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to obey it, and to teach its laws and rules to the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: for: the reason God's hand was on him
decisions.reason: The verse explains verse 9: God favored Ezra because he had given himself to God's law.

decisions.choice: to seek the law: to study it and ask what it requires
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or inquire, often of seeking God (1 Chronicles 16:11). With the law as its object it means to search out its meaning. The three verbs, study, do and teach, set the order of Ezra's life: he learns, he obeys, and then he teaches.

decisions.choice: statute and judgment: the law's fixed rules and its rulings for cases
decisions.reason: The pair sums up the law's commands (Deuteronomy 4:1, 5, 14). Both nouns are singular here, used of the law as a whole.

decisions.choice: study (Balanced, Readable); seek (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Seek the law" can sound like looking for a lost book; "study" says what the verb means with this object. Literal keeps "seek" to show the link with seeking God.

source.text: וְזֶ֣ה׀פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן הַֽנִּשְׁתְּוָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַן֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֔סְתְּא לְעֶזְרָ֥א הַכֹּהֵ֖ן הַסֹּפֵ֑ר סֹפֵ֞ר דִּבְרֵ֧י מִצְוֺת־יְהוָ֛ה וְחֻקָּ֖יו עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And this [is the] copy of the letter which gave the king Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of [the] words of [the] commandments of YHWH and his statutes for Israel:

en.L: And this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the words of the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of his statutes for Israel:
en.B: This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe, an expert in the commandments and statutes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for Israel:
en.R: Here is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra. Ezra was a priest and a teacher of the law. He knew well the commands and laws that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given to Israel. The letter said:

decisions.choice: copy of the letter: a written copy of the royal document
decisions.reason: Both nouns are Persian words for official documents (the first is used again of a copy of a decree in Esther 3:14; 4:8). The narrator says he is quoting the letter as it was issued.

decisions.choice: a scribe of the commandments: one learned in God's law
decisions.reason: The narrator's description goes beyond the king's title in verse 12: Ezra is not a royal secretary but a scholar of the words of God's commands.

decisions.choice: The letter said:
decisions.reason: Readable adds a short line to introduce the letter, since its own sentence about Ezra has become several sentences.

source.text: אַ֨רְתַּחְשַׁ֔סְתְּא מֶ֖לֶךְ מַלְכַיָּ֑א לְעֶזְרָ֣א כָ֠הֲנָא סָפַ֨ר דָּתָ֜א דִּֽי־אֱלָ֧הּ שְׁמַיָּ֛א גְּמִ֖יר וּכְעֶֽנֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: Artaxerxes, king of the kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens, complete; and now

en.L: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven: complete [peace]. And now:
en.B: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
en.R: "From Artaxerxes, the king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the teacher of the law of the God of heaven. Greetings.

decisions.choice: the text changes to Aramaic for the king's letter (7:12-26)
decisions.reason: Here the book changes from Hebrew to Aramaic, the language the Persian empire used for its letters and records, as it did in 4:8-6:18. The letter is quoted in the language in which it was written; at verse 27 the text returns to Hebrew.

decisions.choice: king of kings: a Persian royal title
decisions.reason: Persian kings called themselves "king of kings" in their inscriptions, as rulers over many subject kings. The title is also given to Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 26:7; Daniel 2:37).

decisions.choice: complete: a shortened greeting, "complete [peace]"
decisions.reason: The word means complete or perfect and stands where a letter's greeting goes. It is most likely short for a fuller greeting such as "all peace" (5:7). Some take it with the title before it ("the perfect scribe") or as "and so on", marking that the greeting has been shortened.

decisions.choice: and now: the turn from greeting to business
decisions.reason: Aramaic letters use this word to move from the greeting to the matter in hand (4:10-11, 17).

decisions.choice: Greetings (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for a letter's greeting and leave "and now" unrendered, since a new paragraph does its work. Literal keeps both words.

source.text: מִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י כָל־מִתְנַדַּ֣ב בְּמַלְכוּתִי֩ מִן־עַמָּ֨ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וְכָהֲנ֣וֹהִי וְלֵוָיֵ֗א לִמְהָ֧ךְ לִֽירוּשְׁלֶ֛ם עִמָּ֖ךְ יְהָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: From me is made a decree that every [one] volunteering in my kingdom from the people Israel and its priests and the Levites to go to Jerusalem with you, he may go.

en.L: From me a decree is issued that everyone in my kingdom of the people of Israel and of its priests and Levites who freely offers to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
en.B: I hereby decree that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who choose freely to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
en.R: I order that any Israelites in my kingdom who want to go to Jerusalem may go with you. This includes their priests and Levites.

decisions.choice: volunteering: offering oneself freely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for freewill offerings (verses 15-16; 1:6; 3:5). No one is ordered to go: the return is a free gift, like the silver and gold that go with it.

decisions.choice: from me a decree is made: the formula of a royal decree
decisions.reason: Persian kings issued orders in these words (4:19, 21; 6:8, 11). It gives what follows the force of law.

source.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּי֩ מִן־קֳדָ֨ם מַלְכָּ֜א וְשִׁבְעַ֤ת יָעֲטֹ֨הִי֙ שְׁלִ֔יחַ לְבַקָּרָ֥א עַל־יְה֖וּד וְלִֽירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם בְּדָ֥ת אֱלָהָ֖ךְ דִּ֥י בִידָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because that from before the king and his seven counselors [you are] sent to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem by [the] law of your God which [is] in your hand,

en.L: because you are sent from before the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which is in your hand,
en.B: For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to look into conditions in Judah and Jerusalem by the law of your God, which is in your hand,
en.R: The king and his seven advisers are sending you to find out how well the people in Judah and Jerusalem are keeping the law of your God, which you have with you.

decisions.choice: the king and his seven counselors: the king's inner council
decisions.reason: Persian kings were advised by a council of seven chief nobles (Esther 1:14). The letter has their full authority behind it.

decisions.choice: to inquire by the law: to examine life in Judah against the standard of God's law
decisions.reason: The verb means to look into or investigate (4:15, 19; 5:17). Ezra's task is to see how far the law is being kept, and to set things right (verses 25-26).

decisions.choice: which is in your hand: which you possess and know
decisions.reason: Ezra carries a copy of the law and is also its expert. Verse 25 says the same of "the wisdom of your God which is in your hand".

decisions.choice: how well the people ... are keeping the law
decisions.reason: Readable says what the inquiry is about, which the Aramaic implies by "according to the law".

source.text: וּלְהֵיבָלָ֖ה כְּסַ֣ף וּדְהַ֑ב דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֣א וְיָעֲט֗וֹהִי הִתְנַדַּ֨בוּ֙ לֶאֱלָ֣הּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דִּ֥י בִֽירוּשְׁלֶ֖ם מִשְׁכְּנֵֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and to carry silver and gold which the king and his counselors have freely offered to [the] God of Israel, who in Jerusalem [is] his dwelling,

en.L: and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
en.B: and to take with you the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely given to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
en.R: You are also to take the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have chosen to give to the God of Israel, whose dwelling place is in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem: the king honors Israel's God at his temple
decisions.reason: Persian kings gave gifts to the gods of their subject peoples and asked for their prayers (6:10). The king names God by his people and the place of his temple, as Cyrus did (1:3).

decisions.choice: freely offered: given as a voluntary gift
decisions.reason: The same verb as "volunteer" in verse 13: the king's gift, like the people's journey, is freely given.

source.text: וְכֹל֙ כְּסַ֣ף וּדְהַ֔ב דִּ֣י תְהַשְׁכַּ֔ח בְּכֹ֖ל מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֑ל עִם֩ הִתְנַדָּב֨וּת עַמָּ֤א וְכָֽהֲנַיָּא֙ מִֽתְנַדְּבִ֔ין לְבֵ֥ית אֱלָהֲהֹ֖ם דִּ֥י בִירוּשְׁלֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and all [the] silver and gold which you will find in all [the] province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people and the priests, offering freely for [the] house of their God which [is] in Jerusalem.

en.L: and all the silver and gold that you find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people and the priests, who offer freely for the house of their God which is in Jerusalem.
en.B: along with all the silver and gold you may obtain throughout the province of Babylon, and the freewill offerings of the people and the priests, given willingly for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
en.R: Take also all the silver and gold you can collect in the whole province of Babylon, and the gifts that the people and the priests freely give for the temple of their God in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: find: obtain or collect
decisions.reason: The verb is "find", here of what Ezra is able to receive as gifts in Babylon, from the province's people as well as from the Jews (compare 1:4, 6).

decisions.choice: the freewill offering: a gift given beyond what the law requires
decisions.reason: Freewill offerings were given out of devotion, not by duty (Exodus 35:29; Leviticus 22:18). Ezra 8:25-28 records the weighing of these gifts.

decisions.choice: the temple of their God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house of God throughout the book, so a new reader does not picture a home.

source.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָה֩ אָסְפַּ֨רְנָא תִקְנֵ֜א בְּכַסְפָּ֣א דְנָ֗ה תּוֹרִ֤ין׀דִּכְרִין֙ אִמְּרִ֔ין וּמִנְחָתְה֖וֹן וְנִסְכֵּיה֑וֹן וּתְקָרֵ֣ב הִמּ֔וֹ עַֽל־מַדְבְּחָ֔ה דִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית אֱלָהֲכֹ֖ם דִּ֥י בִירוּשְׁלֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore diligently you will buy with this silver bulls, rams, lambs, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you will offer them on the altar of the house of your God which [is] in Jerusalem.

en.L: Therefore with this silver you shall diligently buy bulls, rams, lambs, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
en.B: With this money, then, you are to buy without fail bulls, rams and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
en.R: Use this money carefully to buy bulls, rams and lambs, along with the grain offerings and drink offerings that go with them. Offer them on the altar of your God's temple in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: diligently: exactly, with care
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian loanword used in royal orders (5:8; 6:8, 12-13; 7:21, 26). It asks that the order be carried out fully and carefully.

decisions.choice: their grain offerings and drink offerings: the gifts that go with each animal offering
decisions.reason: The law sets a grain offering and a drink offering of wine to go with every bull, ram and lamb (Numbers 15:1-12). The king's order follows the law's pattern.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: Silver was the usual means of payment; "this silver" is the money just described.

source.text: וּמָ֣ה דִי֩ עֲלָ֨ךְוְעַל־אֶחָ֜ךְיֵיטַ֗ב בִּשְׁאָ֛ר כַּסְפָּ֥א וְדַהֲבָ֖ה לְמֶעְבַּ֑ד כִּרְע֥וּת אֱלָהֲכֹ֖ם תַּעַבְדֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And whatever to you and to your brothers seems good to do with [the] rest of the silver and the gold, according to [the] will of your God you will do.

en.L: And whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, you shall do according to the will of your God.
en.B: You and your fellow Jews may do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, in keeping with the will of your God.
en.R: You and your fellow Jews may use the rest of the silver and gold in whatever way you think best, as long as it is what your God wants.

decisions.choice: your brothers: your fellow Jews, especially the priests and leaders with you
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means kinsmen, members of the same people, not sons of the same father. Ezra later hands the treasure to priests and Levites (8:24-30).

decisions.choice: according to the will of your God: the king leaves the decision to God's will
decisions.reason: The king sets no rule for the surplus except that it be used as Israel's God would want, a striking deference that Ezra will praise God for (7:27).

decisions.choice: your fellow Jews (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Your brothers" would suggest Ezra's own family; Balanced and Readable say whom it means. Literal keeps "brothers".

source.text: וּמָֽאנַיָּא֙ דִּֽי־מִתְיַהֲבִ֣ין לָ֔ךְ לְפָלְחָ֖ן בֵּ֣ית אֱלָהָ֑ךְ הַשְׁלֵ֕ם קֳדָ֖ם אֱלָ֥הּ יְרוּשְׁלֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the vessels which [are] given to you for [the] service of [the] house of your God, deliver in full before [the] God of Jerusalem.

en.L: And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver them in full before the God of Jerusalem.
en.B: The vessels given to you for the service of the house of your God you must deliver in full to the God of Jerusalem.
en.R: You have also been given bowls and other objects to be used in the worship at your God's temple. Bring all of them safely to the God of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: vessels: bowls, cups and other objects for the temple
decisions.reason: The word covers containers and utensils of every kind. Ezra 8:25-27 lists the silver, gold and bronze objects that were weighed out.

decisions.choice: deliver in full: hand over completely, with nothing missing
decisions.reason: The verb means to complete or to bring safely to an end. Ezra had every item weighed when he set out and again when he arrived (8:26, 33-34).

decisions.choice: the God of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The king names God by the city of his temple, as in verse 15.

decisions.choice: bowls and other objects
decisions.reason: Readable gives an example of what "vessels" means instead of an old word few readers use.

source.text: וּשְׁאָ֗ר חַשְׁחוּת֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱלָהָ֔ךְ דִּ֥י יִפֶּל־לָ֖ךְ לְמִנְתַּ֑ן תִּנְתֵּ֕ן מִן־בֵּ֖ית גִּנְזֵ֥י מַלְכָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] needs of [the] house of your God which falls to you to give, you will give from [the] house of [the] treasures of the king.

en.L: And the rest of the needs of the house of your God, which it falls to you to give, you shall give from the house of the king's treasures.
en.B: Anything else needed for the house of your God that you are responsible for supplying, you may provide from the royal treasury.
en.R: If the temple of your God needs anything else that you must provide, you may pay for it from the king's treasury.

decisions.choice: the house of the king's treasures: the royal treasury
decisions.reason: The costs were met from the royal revenue held in the province, through the treasurers named in the next verse (compare 6:4, 8).

source.text: וּ֠מִנִּי אֲנָ֞ה אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֤סְתְּא מַלְכָּא֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְכֹל֙ גִּזַּֽבְרַיָּ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה דִּ֣י כָל־דִּ֣י יִ֠שְׁאֲלֶנְכוֹן עֶזְרָ֨א כָהֲנָ֜ה סָפַ֤ר דָּתָא֙ דִּֽי־אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א אָסְפַּ֖רְנָא יִתְעֲבִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And from me, I Artaxerxes the king, is made a decree to all the treasurers who [are] in Beyond the River, that all that asks you Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens, diligently let it be done,

en.L: And I, Artaxerxes the king, issue a decree to all the treasurers who are in Beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you shall be done diligently,
en.B: I, King Artaxerxes, issue a decree to all the treasurers in the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you is to be provided in full,
en.R: I, King Artaxerxes, give this order to all the treasurers in the province west of the Euphrates: Give Ezra the priest, the teacher of the law of the God of heaven, whatever he asks of you, and do it with care.

decisions.choice: Beyond the River: the Persian province west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The River is the Euphrates. Seen from Persia, the land beyond it, Syria and the land of Israel, formed one province (4:10-11; 5:3).

decisions.choice: treasurers: the royal finance officials of the province
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian loanword (used of Mithredath in 1:8). The letter in verses 21-24 is addressed to them, not to Ezra: it is a copy of the orders given to the officials who must pay.

decisions.choice: the province west of the Euphrates (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the place name, as it does elsewhere in the book.

source.text: עַד־כְּסַף֮ כַּכְּרִ֣ין מְאָה֒ וְעַד־חִנְטִין֙ כֹּרִ֣ין מְאָ֔ה וְעַד־חֲמַר֙ בַּתִּ֣ין מְאָ֔ה וְעַד־בַּתִּ֥ין מְשַׁ֖ח מְאָ֑ה וּמְלַ֖ח דִּי־לָ֥א כְתָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: up to silver talents one hundred, and up to wheat kors one hundred, and up to wine baths one hundred, and up to baths [of] oil one hundred, and salt which not [is] written.

en.L: up to 100 talents of silver, and up to 100 kors of wheat, and up to 100 baths of wine, and up to 100 baths of oil, and salt without [a] written [limit].
en.B: up to {{units:about 3 3/4 tons of silver|100 talents of silver}}, {{units:about 600 bushels of wheat|100 kors of wheat}}, {{units:about 600 gallons of wine|100 baths of wine}}, {{units:about 600 gallons of olive oil|100 baths of olive oil}}, and salt without limit.
en.R: You may give him up to {{units:about 3 3/4 tons of silver|100 talents of silver}}, {{units:about 600 bushels of wheat|100 kors of wheat}}, {{units:about 600 gallons of wine|100 baths of wine}}, {{units:about 600 gallons of olive oil|100 baths of olive oil}}, and as much salt as he needs.

decisions.choice: talents, kors and baths: the limits of what the treasurers must give
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds, a kor about 6 bushels, a bath about 6 gallons. One hundred talents of silver was a very large sum; the figures set ceilings on Ezra's requests, not amounts to be paid at once.

decisions.choice: salt which is not written: salt without a set limit
decisions.reason: No amount is written down for salt. It was cheap, and every grain offering had to be salted (Leviticus 2:13).

decisions.choice: modern measures, with the original units as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measures in modern terms through the units setting; Literal keeps the ancient units. Oil here is olive oil.

source.text: כָּל־דִּ֗י מִן־טַ֨עַם֙ אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א יִתְעֲבֵד֙ אַדְרַזְדָּ֔א לְבֵ֖ית אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֑א דִּֽי־לְמָ֤ה לֶֽהֱוֵא֙ קְצַ֔ף עַל־מַלְכ֥וּת מַלְכָּ֖א וּבְנֽוֹהִי׃

records.literal_gloss: All that [is] by [the] decree of the God of the heavens, let it be done exactly for [the] house of the God of the heavens, for why should there be wrath on [the] kingdom of the king and his sons?

en.L: Whatever is by the decree of the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?
en.B: Whatever the God of heaven commands for the house of the God of heaven must be done exactly. Why should wrath come upon the realm of the king and his sons?
en.R: Everything the God of heaven commands for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple must be done with care. Otherwise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may become angry with the king's empire and with his sons.

decisions.choice: why should there be wrath: the king fears the anger of Israel's God
decisions.reason: The king's motive is to keep the favor of the God of heaven for his empire and his heirs, as Darius asked for prayers "for the life of the king and his sons" (6:10). The wrath meant is God's.

decisions.choice: exactly: carefully and in full
decisions.reason: Another Persian loanword of royal orders, close in sense to "diligently" (verse 17).

decisions.choice: decree: the same word as for the king's own decree
decisions.reason: The word used for the king's orders (verses 13, 21) is used for the commands of the God of heaven: the king places God's command above his own (compare 6:14).

decisions.choice: he may become angry
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who might be angry, which the Aramaic implies by speaking of wrath after the commands of the God of heaven.

source.text: וּלְכֹ֣ם מְהוֹדְעִ֗ין דִּ֣י כָל־כָּהֲנַיָּ֣א וְ֠לֵוָיֵא זַמָּ֨רַיָּ֤א תָרָֽעַיָּא֙ נְתִ֣ינַיָּ֔א וּפָ֣לְחֵ֔י בֵּ֖ית אֱלָהָ֣א דְנָ֑ה מִנְדָּ֤ה בְלוֹ֙ וַהֲלָ֔ךְ לָ֥א שַׁלִּ֖יט לְמִרְמֵ֥א עֲלֵיהֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to you [we are] making known that all the priests and the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim and [the] servants of this house of God, tribute, tax and toll [it is] not authorized to impose on them.

en.L: And we make known to you that as for all the priests and the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim and the servants of this house of God, it is not permitted to impose tribute, tax or toll on them.
en.B: We also inform you that you have no authority to impose tribute, tax or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants or other workers of this house of God.
en.R: You should also know that you have no right to make any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants or other workers at God's temple pay any kind of tax.

decisions.choice: tribute, tax and toll: the three kinds of royal tax
decisions.reason: The same three terms appear in 4:13, 20. They seem to be a regular tribute in money, a tax on goods or produce, and a toll or land dues; their exact distinctions are not certain. Persian kings sometimes freed temple staff from taxes.

decisions.choice: servants: workers in the temple's service
decisions.reason: The word is from a verb meaning to serve or to worship; it covers all who work in the temple besides those named.

decisions.choice: to you we make known: the king speaks to the treasurers
decisions.reason: "You" is plural, the treasurers of verse 21, and "we" is the king's formal plural.

decisions.choice: any kind of tax (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable sums up the three terms in one phrase, since their differences are not clear and would mean little to new readers.

source.text: וְאַ֣נְתְּ עֶזְרָ֗א כְּחָכְמַ֨ת אֱלָהָ֤ךְ דִּֽי־בִידָךְ֙ מֶ֣נִּי שָׁפְטִ֞ין וְדַיָּנִ֗ין דִּי־לֶהֱוֺ֤ן דָּאיְנִין֙ לְכָל־עַמָּה֙ דִּ֚י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֔ה לְכָל־יָדְעֵ֖י דָּתֵ֣י אֱלָהָ֑ךְ וְדִ֧י לָ֦א יָדַ֖ע תְּהוֹדְעֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, Ezra, according to [the] wisdom of your God which [is] in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who will be judging all the people who [are] in Beyond the River, all knowing [the] laws of your God; and who does not know, you will teach.

en.L: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people who are in Beyond the River, all who know the laws of your God; and whoever does not know them, you shall teach.
en.B: And you, Ezra, by the wisdom of your God that you possess, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River who know the laws of your God. And you are to teach anyone who does not know them.
en.R: And you, Ezra, must use the wisdom your God has given you to choose officials and judges. They are to judge all the people in the province west of the Euphrates who know the laws of your God. And you must teach the laws to anyone who does not know them.

decisions.choice: the wisdom of your God which is in your hand: God's law, which Ezra holds and understands
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes verse 14, "the law of your God which is in your hand". God's law is his wisdom (Deuteronomy 4:6), and Ezra both carries it and knows it.

decisions.choice: all the people ... all who know the laws of your God: the Jews of the province
decisions.reason: The second phrase limits the first: Ezra's judges are for those who belong to Israel's God, wherever they live in the province, not for its other peoples. Those who do not know the law are probably Jews who have not been taught it.

decisions.choice: magistrates and judges: two words for officials who judge
decisions.reason: The first word comes from the verb "to judge" used of Israel's judges; the second is the ordinary Aramaic word for a judge. Together they mean officials who hear and decide cases.

source.text: וְכָל־דִּי־לָא֩ לֶהֱוֵ֨א עָבֵ֜ד דָּתָ֣א דִֽי־אֱלָהָ֗ךְ וְדָתָא֙ דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֔א אָסְפַּ֕רְנָא דִּינָ֕ה לֶהֱוֵ֥א מִתְעֲבֵ֖ד מִנֵּ֑הּ הֵ֤ן לְמוֹת֙ הֵ֣ן לִשְׁרֹשִׁ֔י הֵן־לַעֲנָ֥שׁ נִכְסִ֖ין וְלֶאֱסוּרִֽין׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And anyone who will not be doing the law of your God and the law of the king, diligently judgment let it be done on him, whether to death or to banishment or to confiscation of property or to imprisonment.

en.L: And whoever does not do the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him diligently, whether to death or to banishment or to confiscation of goods or to imprisonment."
en.B: Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must be punished without fail, whether by death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment."
en.R: Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must be punished at once. The punishment may be death, being sent away from the land, losing property, or prison."

decisions.choice: the law of your God and the law of the king: God's law given the king's backing
decisions.reason: For the Jews of the province, the law of Moses now carries the authority of the Persian crown. Disobeying it is also disobeying the king.

decisions.choice: banishment: being rooted out, cut off from the community
decisions.reason: The word comes from "root" and means uprooting. It most likely means exile or being cut off from the people (compare 10:8). Some take it as a corporal punishment, such as flogging.

decisions.choice: confiscation of property: a fine on one's goods
decisions.reason: Literally "a penalty of goods": the seizure of possessions, as in 10:8.

decisions.choice: being sent away from the land
decisions.reason: Readable explains banishment in plain words.

source.text: בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן כָּזֹאת֙ בְּלֵ֣ב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְפָאֵ֕ר אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH [the] God of our fathers, who has put [a thing] like this in [the] heart of the king, to beautify the house of YHWH which [is] in Jerusalem,

en.L: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this into the heart of the king, to beautify the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which is in Jerusalem,
en.B: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our ancestors, who put it into the king's heart to bring honor to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem,
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our ancestors! He made the king want to bring honor to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the text returns to Hebrew, and Ezra speaks for himself
decisions.reason: After the Aramaic letter (7:12-26) the book returns to Hebrew. Ezra now speaks in the first person ("our", "me", "I"), and his own account runs to the end of chapter 9.

decisions.choice: who has put this in the king's heart: God moved the king
decisions.reason: Ezra gives the credit for the king's decree to God, as the book does for Cyrus (1:1) and Darius (6:22). Compare Proverbs 21:1: the king's heart is in the LORD's hand.

decisions.choice: to beautify: to adorn, to make glorious
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God glorifying his house and his people (Isaiah 60:7, 13). The temple was already built (6:15); the king's gifts adorn it and supply its worship.

decisions.choice: Praise (Readable); Blessed be (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Blessed be" is the usual form of praise in Hebrew prayer, but to most new readers "bless" sounds like something done to a person. Readable says "Praise".

decisions.choice: ancestors (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forefathers of the people, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

source.text: וְעָלַ֣י הִטָּה־חֶ֗סֶד לִפְנֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְיֽוֹעֲצָ֔יו וּלְכָל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַגִּבֹּרִ֑ים וַאֲנִ֣י הִתְחַזַּ֗קְתִּי כְּיַד־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהַי֙ עָלַ֔י וָאֶקְבְּצָ֧ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֛ל רָאשִׁ֖ים לַעֲל֥וֹת עִמִּֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and to me has extended steadfast love before the king and his counselors and to all the officials of the king, the mighty. And I, I strengthened myself according to [the] hand of YHWH my God upon me, and I gathered from Israel heads to go up with me.

en.L: and who has extended steadfast love to me before the king and his counselors and before all the mighty princes of the king. And I took courage, according to the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
en.B: and who has shown me faithful love before the king, his counselors and all the king's powerful officials. Because the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God was on me, I took courage and gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.
en.R: He showed me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love when I stood before the king, his advisers and all the king's powerful leaders. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God was helping me, so I was encouraged. I gathered leaders from Israel to go with me to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: God's loyal, faithful kindness
decisions.reason: The word is God's covenant love, his faithfulness to his people. Ezra sees it in the favor he found at the Persian court (compare 9:9).

decisions.choice: I strengthened myself: I took courage
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow strong or be encouraged. Ezra's confidence rests on God's hand, not on the king's letter (8:22).

decisions.choice: heads: the heads of families
decisions.reason: The leaders who went with Ezra were the heads of the ancestral families listed in 8:1-14.

decisions.choice: the hand of YHWH my God upon me
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 6. Ezra now uses the refrain of himself.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for the king's high officials is rendered as the book does elsewhere.
